top_choice_rationale: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a general method whose adoption is verifiable in medicinal and process chemistry, materials and total synthesis. Its generality came from catalyst design aimed at the steps specific to this bond (amine binding, beta-hydride elimination, difficult C-N reductive elimination from amido complexes), solved independently by Buchwald and Hartwig over three decades, so the two-name allocation and a narrow citation are well defined. P001 is a strong, mature chemical invention (reversible terminators and clustered templates) and ranks second, clearly ahead of no award.
